title: suderra.time-state.v1 authenticated clock state
description: What root knows about the clock and the agent may rely on (ADR-048 DEC-7.2, DEC-7.3, DEC-7.5): written atomically by the root time helper to /run/suderra/time-state (root:suderra, 0640) from chrony's tracking data and the persisted time floor, and read by the agent, which cannot read adjtimex under ProtectClock. The agent's clock authority is this document and nothing else: it holds freshness-dependent actuation while state is not a synced one and never lets local control, safe-state or alarms depend on time. `synced-nts` is a clock chrony disciplines against pinned NTS servers; `synced-unauthenticated` is a clock disciplined by a site NTP server the signed site policy explicitly marked as not NTS-capable; `unsynced` is everything else, including a clock that only passed the time floor. The state is a claim of the writer's last write, so channels.json time bounds how old updated_at may be and says which state each consumer needs.

floor_at.description: The time floor in force: max(build timestamp, persisted last-good time) (DEC-7.2). The clock never reads earlier than this once the floor helper ran.

last_sync_at.description: Instant of the last synchronization chrony reported (its tracking reference time); null while the clock has not synchronized since boot.

offset_ms.description: Last measured offset of the system clock from its time source in milliseconds, rounded, signed; null while unsynced.

updated_at.description: The helper's clock at the write. The helper rewrites the document at least every channels.json time.refresh_seconds; a reader that finds it more than time.max_age_seconds away from its own clock treats the state as unsynced (channels.json time.stale_rule).
